content.scenario: A consumer, Kumar, files a complaint against a company for selling him a defective product. The District Commission requires a sample of the goods to determine whether the goods suffer from any defect alleged in the complaint.
content.outcome: The District Commission has the power to obtain a sample of the goods from the complainant, seal it, and authenticate it, and refer the sample to the appropriate laboratory for analysis or test, as per Section 38(2)(c) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

user_queries: What is the purpose of obtaining a sample of goods in a consumer complaint?
Can the District Commission require a sample of goods from the complainant?
How does the District Commission use the sample of goods to determine the defect?
